etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from French crayon (“pencil”), from craie (“chalk”) + -on (“(diminutive)”), from Latin creta (“chalk, clay”), from crētus.

definitions.definition: A stick of colored chalk or wax used for drawing.
A colored pencil, a colouring pencil

quote.citation: 1695, C[harles] A[lphonse] du Fresnoy, translated by John Dryden, De Arte Graphica. The Art of Painting, […], London:  […]  J[ohn] Heptinstall for W. Rogers, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Let no day pass over you  […]  without giving some strokes of the pencil or the crayon.

definitions.definition: (dated) A crayon drawing, or a drawing with colored lines.

quote.text: But on the wall hung two fine crayons, representing Louis XVI. and Marie Antoinette — pictures which she recognized as having hung in the corridor of the Tuileries — and in front of them were burning two candles on a species of rude altar.

definitions.definition: (dated) A pencil of carbon used in producing electric light.
(transitive, intransitive) To draw with a crayon.

pronunciation: US, uncommon, especially Northeastern US, Midwestern US
US, rare, especially Philadelphia, New Jersey, sometimes Southern US
